summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis was admitted with severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the right upper quadrant and back. Initial concern for peritonitis was ruled out by peritoneal fluid analysis showing no infection. Imaging showed no abscess or obstruction. Elevated liver enzymes and a history of medication use pointed to a toxic liver injury from statin and fibrate therapy, which were discontinued. The patient also experienced difficulty draining his peritoneal dialysis catheter, requiring two days of hemodialysis and a successful wire clearance procedure. His pain resolved, labs improved, and he was discharged home with adjusted insulin therapy and close follow-up planned.
problems: Mechanical complication due to peritoneal dialysis catheter
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Antilipemic and antiarteriosclerotic drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
